body:
> This is [apparently](https://www.reddit.com/r/godot/comments/1ikrij3/notifications_reference_in_43/) not considered a problem because they're on different classes, and thus a single scene won't be getting both.

This was regarded to be generally a non-issue in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/12304

> As far as I can tell there's no good reason for this; it's not like we're going to run out of numbers.

Some of these are likely the way they are due to old API and bad foresight. Others correspond to each other by design (such as MainLoop and Node's `NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_PAUSED`)
Changing the corresponding values of these constants _now_ would break compatibility and expectations.

Well it's certainly causing an issue for me, as it's making it harder for me to locate documentation on the specific notifications I'm getting. I cannot trust that if I see a specific number, and I find documentation about that number as a notification, that the documentation is actually talking about the notification I'm looking at.

In general "this has zero benefit and it has a low but nonzero cost" is not an argument in favor of the status quo, and I'm not sure why people frequently present it as though it were.

Fixing this now would only break projects that check for notification equality using the underlying numbers rather than the constants. That's not how you're supposed to use constants, so I expect this would be a negligibly small fraction of projects, and they'd have only themselves to blame for not using the intended reference method.

Hey! I understand  why you opened an issue, but this is better discussed in a proposal (https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues) since this isn't a bug, but rather a change in design/feature. The proposal flow will also help us identify whether making notifications unique is the right tool for the job - or if we can improve documentation, and so on.

> In general "this has zero benefit and it has a low but nonzero cost" is not an argument in favor of the status quo, and I'm not sure why people frequently present it as though it were.
>
> Fixing this now would only break projects that check for notification equality using the underlying numbers rather than the constants. That's not how you're supposed to use constants, so I expect this would be a negligibly small fraction of projects, and they'd have only themselves to blame for not using the intended reference method.

When considering compatibility, it's important to not only focus on GDScript _code_ itself but the entire ecosystem. There are a wide range of scenarios where changing enum values would break existing projects, for example:
- The value is serialized on the disk and read by a different Godot version
- The value is sent over network and read by someone with a different Godot version
- GDExtension uses the value

The last point is particularly important, as the GDExtension API maintains binary compatibility down to Godot 4.1. This is necessary so that extensions written in older engine versions can still be run in newer versions. Changing enumerators would break that expectation and introduce exactly the hard-to-trace bugs you're describing.

---

Concerning this specific problem, I brought it up in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/75839. We did in fact fix the worst offender (`NOTIFICATION_NODE_RECACHE_REQUESTED`). For others, it's less of a problem because they appear in disjoint inheritance hierarchies. Note that I'm not saying it's _no_ problem -- I brought up the same issue, after all -- but that breaking compatibility now would likely be more surprising than sticking with the values.

I hope that helps shedding some light on the topic! 🙂

@Bromeon That makes sense as to why fixing it right away would be a problem, thanks. It doesn't change the fact that IMO this should, at some point, be fixed. Perhaps not in 4.5 but in 5.0 when breaking changes are more acceptable.
